probe.question: Can TomP2P use an exact raw 160-bit Git SHA-1 object id as the caller-supplied DHT location key without mandatory hashing/transformation or external namespace mapping, while retrieval exposes data that could be locally Git-hash verified?

observations: TomP2P Number160 is explicitly a 160-bit number.
Number160 has constructors from byte[] and from a 40-character hexadecimal string, so a caller can construct the 160-bit value directly instead of invoking createHash(String).
Peer.get accepts a Number160 locationKey directly; the public API therefore does not require an additional hash or namespace transformation before lookup.
FutureDHT exposes Data, evaluated data maps, and raw data from get(), so retrieved payload bytes/data are available to the caller for local verification in principle.

No passive DHT lookup was issued and no independently pre-existing residency of a target canonical Git object in a reachable TomP2P network was established. No returned canonical Git bytes were available to hash-check in this slice.
probe.inference: TomP2P passes the source-level exact native key-width/binding test: a raw 20-byte Git SHA-1 can be represented directly as Number160 and passed to get(Number160) without a mandatory extra hashing step. It does not pass the complete Phase-1 bridge criterion because independently pre-existing target residency and actual canonical Git-byte retrieval remain unproven. Local Git hash verification is mechanically possible only if such canonical bytes are actually returned.
probe.tested_scope: TomP2P public primary API/project semantics for Number160 construction, DHT get location key, and retrieval result exposure; source-level audit only. No network GET/PUT, publication, hosted query/project, mapping service, or target-residency test.

assumptions_uncertainty_residuals.assumption: A 20-byte Git SHA-1 is supplied directly to Number160 rather than passed through createHash(String), which intentionally hashes a string with SHA-1.
assumptions_uncertainty_residuals.uncertainty: The public API establishes key compatibility but does not establish that any relevant public/reachable TomP2P DHT already contains the target Git object under that exact key.
assumptions_uncertainty_residuals.residual: Need independently pre-existing residency plus actual canonical bytes from a passive retrieval before local Git object-hash verification can close the bridge.
